stories.author: TangerineDream
stories.title: Saving 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1's DNS cache
stories.groq_label: Caching unparsed wire-format DNS records in contiguous memory buffers instead of pre-parsed Rust objects saved Cloudflare 100 terabytes of RAM.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Detailed:

This blog post focuses on solving high memory overhead in Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS cache. The Hacker News discussion suggests that commenters were primarily impressed by practical low-level memory optimizations, especially storing raw byte buffers rather than fully parsed representations, which many believed could significantly improve cache density and lookup performance. At the same time, the discussion repeatedly highlighted concerns about potential safety trade-offs and implementation nuances, with commenters debating issues such as bypassing Rust safety checks when using manually calculated offsets in flat vectors, memory alignment of deserialized data, and whether alternative architectures like in-RAM databases or C-style inline allocations might be superior. While there was no unanimous agreement on every aspect, the overall impression was that the project introduces an interesting idea that would benefit from further refinement.

stories.groq_explain: Emacs 31 introduced an experimental built-in Markdown mode called markdown-ts-mode that uses Tree-sitter for parsing.
